adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:35 — from_dict quietly returns None on TypeError/ValueError (for example an unknown or renamed key from a newer producer during a deploy), which turns off cycle prevention with no log or metric, so the sync echoes back to the source integration unnoticed.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict` the diff shows a broad `except (ValueError, TypeError): return None`, which will silently drop `assignment_source_dict` when the payload has missing/extra/renamed keys (e.g., a newer producer including an additional field causes `TypeError` in `cls(**input_dict)`). Downstream, `sync_assignee_outbound` passes this parsed value into `installation.should_sync(..., parsed_assignment_source)`, and `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only prevents cycles when `sync_source` is non-None and the integration IDs match. If parsing returns None, the cycle-prevention check is bypassed with no logging/metric. This is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/observability gap, but not a guaranteed defect in the current code path because the dict is typically produced by `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` in the same codebase.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — The cycle check compares integration IDs, not external issues, so a group linked to two issues on the same integration (for example Jira APP-1 and APP-2) no longer syncs to APP-2 after an inbound change on APP-1, which is a regression from the old behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync()` that returns `False` when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (issues.py). The outbound assignee sync passes a single `assignment_source` (derived from the inbound integration) through `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign` → `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` → `sync_assignee_outbound` task, and `should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` gates the sync. Because the check is only by integration id (not by external issue id), an inbound change from one linked issue on a given integration will suppress outbound syncing to all other linked issues on that same integration, matching the reported regression scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:115 — Only the direct echo to the source is blocked: when integration A changes X->Y quickly, B's delayed echo of X comes back tagged source=B, differs from Y, and is pushed out to A again, so assignment flaps between two integrations.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only blocks outbound sync when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (see `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(...)`), i.e., it prevents direct self-echo cycles but explicitly allows “other integrations to propagate changes outward” (comment in the diff). Given `sync_group_assignee_inbound()` now tags assignments with `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)` and that source is forwarded through `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` → task kwargs → `installation.should_sync(...)`, a delayed inbound update from integration B could still trigger outbound propagation to integration A because the source won’t match A’s integration id. Whether this causes real assignment flapping depends on external timing/ordering not shown in the diff, so it’s a scope/edge-case concern rather than a verifiable defect in the patch itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:28 — to_dict puts a raw datetime into the celery kwargs; under a JSON serializer it comes back as an ISO string, and from_dict stores it in `queued` without coercion, so the typed datetime field quietly holds a str.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` the code uses `asdict(self)`, which will include `queued` as a `datetime` object (see `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` in the dataclass). That dict is passed through Celery task kwargs (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(... assignment_source_dict=assignment_source.to_dict())`).
